name: Forged wrought iron (the smith's ornament and saddle bars)
process: The smith heats wrought-iron bar in the forge and works it on the anvil: drawing tapers, scrolling, bending rings over a mandrel, splitting and upsetting, and joining pieces by forge-welding (the iron's own slag acts as the flux) or with collars and rivets. Leaves and flowers are cut from sheet, veined with chisels and dished. At Oxford the capitals of the iron clusters carry wrought-iron flowers and foliage and the spandrels are wrought-iron branches; in Albion the smith's work is the rings in the arcade spandrels and the saddle bars that stiffen the leaded lights.
